content.title: Response to Reviewer Uy7S
content.comment:
Thank you for your feedback. Below, we address your weaknesses/questions.

Q1: My main concern with this paper is that it seems that the authors do not present their novelties in a quite clear manner. Specifically, from what I understand, the novelty of this paper should lie in how the unbiased knowledge distillation is conducted through meta-learning so that the unrealistic prior unbiased set can be removed, but not lie in the pipeline of meta-learning. However, it seems that the authors focus a lot on explaining the meta-learning, but not their specific designs. For example, I hope the authors can discuss more on their equation 8, and how they made it to be data-driven. From my guess, I think equation 8 is how the unbiased distillation criterion is established, which is the part that is interesting in this paper. However, the lack of details there makes me very confused.

A1: Generally, vanilla meta-learning consists of three steps: Virtual-Train, Meta-Train, and Actual-Train.
It reveals in previous work that over 80% of total computation costs come from backward step of Meta-Train, and meta gradient is computed with respect to the loss on a prior unbiased set. Xu et al reveal that over 80% of the total computation comes from the Meta-Train backward step in which meta gradient is computed with respect to the loss on a prior unbiased set. Therefore, to efficiently compute meta gradient, we propose a novel meta update rule via policy gradient to obtain the approximated meta gradient. Specifically, we introduce gradient-distribution consistency to constrain the gradient of KD loss and unbiased training loss to optimize the outer loop.

Q2: Besides, correct me if I miss it, but does this paper only demonstrate its efficiency through experiments but does not provide any discussion or analysis w.r.t. why this efficiency is achieved? While the decrease in computational overhead looks quite impressive through experiments, I hope the authors can discuss or analyze this but not only observe this.

A2: As mentioned in equation 6, 

Q3: Besides, while I do have a feeling that this paper combines knowledge distillation and meta-learning in a way that is different from previous papers, I do suggest the authors at least discuss the difference between this paper and the previous works that combine knowledge distillation and meta-learning in their related work.

A3: Thank you for your advice, it is necessary to discuss the connection between KD and Meta-Learning and review the previous work.

content.title: Response to Reviewer ZZYi
content.comment:
We sincerely appreciate your positive feedback! Below, we address the questions and concerns you raised in the comments.

Q1: In table 6, the authors only show the average running time per training iteration, but do not provide the number of iterations. These results cannot support the claim of "save about 6 times training time". The authors had better provide the total training time. Besides, it seems that "save 6 time training time" is not a proper expression. Maby "reduce to xx%" is better.
A1: As we report in the experiment details, our proposed method is trained on 300 epochs with a batch size of 128. The total training time is also less than the comparison method.

Q2: Below Eq. 8, "(see Figure 3(c) and Figure 4 for ablation studies", Fig.4 is not in the main paper. The authors had better to point out it in the appendix.
A2: Thank you for your advice, we will point this out better in the main paper to make it clear.

content.title: Response to Reviewer LU8E
content.comment:
We sincerely appreciate your positive feedback! Below, we address the questions and concerns you raised in the comments.

Q1: In section 1 the author discusses why the proposed method can be more efficient than other meta learning based methods but doesn’t justify why it can improve accuracy than existing meta-learning based methods. The higher empirical results lacks analysis and justification.The higher empirical results lacks analysis and justification.

A1: As we discussed at the end of section 3. In this work, we propose a learning-based approach that learns Rt(c) by employing a meta-learning optimization strategy. Intuitively, the prior unbiased set reflects the finite field classes distribution, which is biased from the real distribution, while estimating the unbiased sample from the training sample provides a path to approximate the real distribution. It is worth noting that the teacher and student networks have different learning routes, so the outputs of the two models will not increasingly become consistent.

Q2: The writing of section 3 is kind of hard to follow. At the beginning, the model and algorithm details are described but I cannot see why and how the proposed method can handle label noise. At the end of this section, I think the method works because of the unbiased knowledge distillation, but there is no justification that the why the distilled knowledge is unbiased.

A2: In this work, we propose a learning-based approach that learns Rt(c) by employing a meta-learning optimization strategy. Intuitively, the prior unbiased set reflects the finite field classes distribution, which is biased from the real distribution, while estimating the unbiased sample from the training sample provides a path to approximate the real distribution. This is reason that our method is outperform to other methods. 

Q3: The technical detail should be double checked, e.g. Eqn. (8) is important as it is about unbiased knowledge distillation. The symbols used are confusing. Are R(t), R_c(t) and R_t(c) the same thing? Why it helps extract the unbiased knowledge?

A3: R_t(c) reflects the selection criterion of class c at time step t. we formalize R_c(t) as a selection criterion for c classes.

Q4: Theoretical insights are provided for algorithm convergence analysis. It would be better to compare with other meta learning-based methods in terms of theoretical convergence (if any of the previous works have). This can make the efficiency improvement contribution more persuasive.

A4: There is indeed a lot of work that does not provide algorithmic complexity analysis, and we see this as future work.

Q5: A minor point is although many related literatures are cited, it doesn’t review sufficient most recent works (published in 2022) on learning with label noise and do comparison with these methods. To name a few,

A5: Thank you for your suggestion. These efforts will be discussed in the next release.

content.title: About: experiments on Clothing 1M dataset and the novelty of our work
content.comment:
We thanks for the reviewer's feedbacks. As a very quick rebuttal, it would be much appreciated if the reviewer tZqU double-check our paper, and we indeed have the experimental results on Clothing 1M dataset in Tab. 5 of our initial submission. And our results are quite competitive on this large-scale dataset.

About the novelty of this paper, We extend the idea of knowledge distillation to the meta-learning paradigm, and propose the dual-level distribution consistency to optimize teacher-student networks. 
**This is very different from the EMA or EMA-based work that you mentioned, where teachers are learnable and optimized through an outer loop instead of by moving parameters.**
by the way, in order to reduce the computational complexity, we refine the inner loop adaption and outer loop optimization of the meta-learning paradigm respectively.

In addition, inner loop adaptions and outer loop optimization are also introduced to this work to help reduce the number of the iteration.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1.The proposed approach has demonstrated the improvement over other approaches on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 dataset.

Weakness:
1.This work is to solve learning with noise problem. However, the motivation is not clear, like the reason why this pipeline can help solve this problem is missing. E.g., why we need to apply teacher-student framework to solve this problem and how it can be robust to the data noise during the training stage, especially in the early training stage. 
2.The evaluation data is relatively small, it would be much more convincing to run additional experiments on other popular large dataset, like Clothing1M dataset.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The novelty is marginal. The teacher student network has been adopted to the learning with noise data for a very long time, for example,   Mean teachers are better role models: Weight averaged consistency targets improve semi-supervised deep learning results NIPS 2017 and latest work Training Better Deep Neural Networks with Uncertainty Mining Net in BMVC 2021. The authors also did not further discuss why teacher-student network is robust to the data noise, especially in the early training stage.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper has demonstrated the improvement over listed benchmarks, However, more experiments are needs, especially the comparison on other popular large datasets. The motivation part is also not clear.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes an efficient meta-learning method for learning with noisy labels. Specifically, the authors present a dynamic strategy to select unbiased samples (removing noisy samples) for meta-training. Furthermore, a pipeline of inner loop adaption and outer loop optimization is proposed to reduce the training time. Extensive results demonstrate the proposed method achieves comparable or even better performance, with less time.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
1. This paper proposes a novel efficient optimization-based pipeline to address the noisy samples in meta-learning.  The most attractive point of this paper is the reduction of training time. The proposed method only takes 1/6 of training time while achieving comparable or even better performance. Training time is one of the key factors for practical applications, but it always is ignored in academic papers. An efficient solution will narrow the gap between academic papers and practical applications.
 
2. It is interesting to incorporate knowledge distillation (KD) with meta-feedback to obtain efficient learning with noisy labels. This is a novel solution since usually KD is used for model compression not for reducing training time. It is also a new idea in the field of meta-learning. Thus, I think it will bring some new insights for efficient meta-learning.

3. The authors provide theoretical proofs to analyze the convergence and complexity, which make the proposed method more solid. Besides, the experimental results on CIFAR10/100 clearly demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method with impressive speedup in training.

Weaknesses

1. In table 6, the authors only show the average running time per training iteration, but do not provide the number of iterations. These results cannot support the claim of "save about 6 times training time". The authors had better provide the total training time. Besides, it seems that "save 6 time training time" is not a proper expression. Maby "reduce to xx%" is better.

2. Below Eq. 8, "(see Figure 3(c) and Figure 4 for ablation studies", Fig.4 is not in the main paper. The authors had better to point out it in the appendix.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The main idea is novel and interesting. 
This paper is clear and easy to understand. 
The authors provide algorithms in detail for reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper proposes a novel efficient meta-learning pipeline for learning with noisy labels. The idea combined with knowledge distillation is interesting and the extensive experimental results clearly demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Strength:
1. From my perspective, while there are certain existing works to incorporate knowledge distillation into meta-learning, the proposed method seems to be still interesting.
2. The description of the challenges that existing methods face and how the authors aim to deal with those challenges is clear.

Weaknesses:
1. My main concern with this paper is that it seems that the authors do not present their novelties in a quite clear manner. Specifically, from what I understand, the novelty of this paper should lie in how the unbiased knowledge distillation is conducted through meta-learning so that the unrealistic prior unbiased set can be removed, but not lie in the pipeline of meta-learning. However, it seems that the authors focus a lot on explaining the meta-learning, but not their specific designs. For example, I hope the authors can discuss more on their equation 8, and how they made it to be data-driven. From my guess, I think equation 8 is how the unbiased distillation criterion is established, which is the part that is interesting in this paper. However, the lack of details there makes me very confused.
2. Besides, correct me if I miss it, but does this paper only demonstrate its efficiency through experiments but does not provide any discussion or analysis w.r.t. why this efficiency is achieved? While the decrease in computational overhead looks quite impressive through experiments, I hope the authors can discuss or analyze this but not only observe this.
3. Besides, while I do have a feeling that this paper combines knowledge distillation and meta-learning in a way that is different from previous papers, I do suggest the authors at least discuss the difference between this paper and the previous works that combine knowledge distillation and meta-learning in their related work.

content.title: Efficiently Meta-Learning for Robust Deep Networks without Prior Unbiased Set
content.abstract: Learning with noisy labels is a practically challenging problem in robust deep learning. Recent efforts to improve the robustness are made by meta-learning the sample weights or transition matrix from a prior unbiased set. Thus, previous meta-learning based approaches generally assume the existence of such prior unbiased set. Unfortunately, this assumption unrealistically simplifies the task of learning noisy labels in real-world scenarios; even worse the updating iterations in previous meta-learning algorithms typically demand prohibitive computational cost. This paper proposes an efficient meta-learning approach for robust deep learning to address these challenges. Specifically, without relying on prior unbiased validation set, our method dynamically estimates unbiased samples in training data and leverages meta-learning to refine the deep networks. Furthermore, to significantly reduce the updating iterations in optimization cost, we elaborately design the inner loop adaption and outer loop optimization of the meta-learning paradigm, respectively. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach is able to save about 6 times training time while achieving comparable or even better generalization performance. In particular, we improve accuracy on the CIFAR100 benchmark at 40% instance-dependent noise by more than 13% in absolute accuracy.
